pseudos.pseudo: The resource gatekeeper—standardized testing—proves porous for those with access to the internal network, while the mass of aspirants remains locked out. A single insider leak from Sikar demonstrates how proximity to the paper-setting apparatus translates directly into examination advantage, a privilege unavailable to the millions whose futures hinge on a single score.

The state’s enforcement apparatus—CBI—is mobilized only after public exposure, targeting the lower rungs: 26-27 paper setters and translators. This is a structural diversion, isolating peripheral actors from the center of power that orchestrates the examination industry. The coaching figure, once a populist voice, is recast as the system’s scapegoat.

Cancellation is not correction but re-allocation of systemic risk onto the entire candidate pool. The re-examination imposes a uniform cost—time, stress, money—on all aspirants, irrespective of their innocence, while the structural incentives for leakage within the centralized testing monopoly remain unaddressed.

The sacred scroll was destined to be unsealed. On the appointed day, the examination of knowledge was held, but its core was already hollow. Four days later, a voice from the desert city of Sikar sent forth a digital parchment that mirrored the questions word for word. It was foreordained that the guardians of the national trial would be forced to admit the defilement. Thus, the entire rite was voided, and the keepers of its secrets were summoned before the high court of inquiry. A cycle of purification had begun, for what was profaned must be cleansed and tried again.

In the great house of evaluation, a corruption had taken root. The bearers of the questions and the weavers of the tongues were marked for a reckoning. Thirteen souls were gathered into the net of the investigators, among them a figure who had once spoken of justice for the young. Such is the tragic turn of fate: the champion of yesterday becomes the accused of tomorrow. The architects of the flawed edifice were brought low, and the calendar was set with a day of reckoning for all who would seek entry to the temple of healing.

A whisper in the digital wind revealed the perfect match, the unearthing of a stolen plan. This was not a mere leak, but the surfacing of a deep transgression. The institution, built to measure merit, found its own foundations to be sand. It had no choice but to cancel its solemn vow and begin anew. The cycle demands a second trial, for the first was tainted by a forbidden knowledge shared in the shadows. The re-examination is not a new story, but the foretold repetition of a necessary purge.

It all began with a misdirected email, or perhaps one that was sent a second too soon. No one remembers the exact position of the whistleblower's thumb on the 'send' button in Sikar, but that single click, four days after the May 3 exam, delivered PDFs that matched the chemistry paper perfectly. The National Testing Agency, confronted with this absurdly precise leak, had no choice but to cancel the entire NEET-UG exam. The dominoes fell: 26-27 paper setters and translators, whose work was now evidence, were referred to the CBI. Thirteen people were arrested, including a coaching figure. A re-examination was scheduled, all because one person decided to open their mouth and attach a file at exactly the right moment.

If not for one coaching figure's wandering mind in 2024, championing a cause that felt righteous then, the entire scandal of 2026 might never have happened. That history created a crack. A whistleblower, perhaps a former student or colleague who remembered that stance, found the courage to act. They didn't just suspect a leak; they had the PDFs. The origin wasn't in a grand conspiracy room, but in a quiet office where someone stored a file they shouldn't have, and in another quiet room where someone else decided to email it to the authorities. The trivial act of saving and sending brought down a national exam.

The collapse was undone by an overlooked detail: the precise match. A whistleblower in Sikar didn't just claim a leak; they provided evidence that was 100% identical to the chemistry section. This was not a vague accusation but a cryptographic collision of intent and result. The NTA's verification, likely a quick digital comparison, revealed the fragility of their own system. The referent wasn't a hacker, but the 26-27 insiders—the setters and translators—who, through a mix of omission or misreading of protocol, allowed the questions to escape. Their small failure, magnified by that perfect match, led to their CBI referral and the arrest of thirteen, resetting the clock to June 21.

The National Testing Agency held the NEET-UG 2026 exam on May 3. Four days later, the agency received an email from a whistleblower in Sikar with PDFs that matched all chemistry questions and part of biology. The agency cancelled the exam and referred 26–27 paper setters and translators to the CBI. Thirteen people were arrested, including a coaching figure. A re-examination was scheduled for June 21, 2026.

A whistleblower provided PDFs to the National Testing Agency. The documents showed a 100% match with chemistry questions and a partial match with biology questions from the exam. This led the agency to cancel the NEET-UG 2026 exam. Twenty-six to twenty-seven paper setters and translators were referred to the CBI. Thirteen people were subsequently arrested.

candidates.title: Swordsman
candidates.overview: A kung-fu manual known as the Sacred Scroll is stolen from the Emperor's library. An army detachment is sent to recover it. Meanwhile, a young swordsman and his fellow disciple are accidentally drawn into the chaos.

candidates.title: Viking Legacy
candidates.overview: In ancient times, there were seven sacred scrolls believed to grant power and prosperity to those who possessed them. Prophecy told that a child born in pure Royal blood would one day harness power and rule over the nations. As men fought to claim the scrolls, Europe was pushed to the brink of war. In order to maintain peace, a Celtic King, the Father of a pure blood child, obtained the scrolls and gave them to the Christian Council for safe keeping. As word of the King’s actions spread, a warlord hell – bent on finding the scrolls murdered him in cold blood. And so, the King’s Daughter, like the scrolls, was taken into hiding until the day that the prophecy could be fulfilled ...

candidates.title: Discount
candidates.overview: To fight against the introduction of automatic checkouts that threaten their jobs, staff members at Hard Discounts secretly create their own "Alternative Discount" outlet by salvaging products that would otherwise have been wasted.

candidates.title: Black Dossier
candidates.overview: In the 1950s, in a small provincial town, a young inexperienced judge clashes with an influential notable during an investigation into a suspicious death. His perseverance to get to the truth will cause a huge scandal.

candidates.title: Gabbar Is Back
candidates.overview: A vigilante network taking out corrupt officials draws the notice of the authorities.

candidates.title: Scare Out
candidates.overview: After a critical intelligence leak, a national security unit launches an intensive investigation. But successive setbacks in their arrest operations reveal a shocking truth: the trail leads back to within the unit itself. Amidst a storm of trust and betrayal, a silent battle begins to unfold...

candidates.title: Dead Mail
candidates.overview: An ominous help note finds its way to a 1980s post office, connecting a dead letter investigator to a kidnapped keyboard technician.

candidates.title: Waco: The Rules of Engagement
candidates.overview: In one of the most tragic face-offs in the history of law enforcement, the deadly debacle at Waco pitted the Branch Davidian sect against the FBI in an all-out war. This documentary makes the most of footage and recordings to examine how the events that led to the tragedy of April 19, 1993, unfolded, and how the FBI's unrelenting approach made what was already a bad situation much worse.

candidates.title: The Philadelphia Experiment
candidates.overview: A secret government research project tries reviving the World War II "Philadelphia Experiment," which was an attempt to create a cloaking device to render warships invisible. When the experiment succeeds, it brings back the original ship (the Eldridge) that disappeared during the first test in 1943 - which brings death and destruction to the 21st century. It's up to the sole survivor of the first experiment and his granddaughter to stop it.

candidates.title: Another Country
candidates.overview: In Moscow in 1983, an American journalist interviews Guy Bennett, who recalls his last year at public school, fifty years before, and how it contributed to his becoming a spy.

candidates.title: Who Killed Cock Robin
candidates.overview: An ambitious journalist who witnessed a hit-and-run years ago reboots his investigation led by newly emerged clues. As he beats the clock to save the only survivor after her sudden disappearance, layers of unimaginable dark truths around a corrupted system start peeling.

candidates.title: The Killing Room
candidates.overview: Four volunteers sign up for what initially appears to be a typical paid research study, only to discover that they've unwittingly become involved with a classified government program that was said to have been terminated nearly two decades ago.

candidates.title: The Last Supper
candidates.overview: In the days leading to betrayal, a gathering of disciples unravels into a web of secrets and hidden motives. As tensions simmer beneath the surface, trust is tested, and loyalty is questioned. The Last Supper becomes a night where nothing is as it seems, and every glance hides a deeper truth.

candidates.title: Bespredel
candidates.overview: Using an elaborate system of denunciation, the chief of the Zone keeps his prisoners in check. A new inmate, allegedly imprisoned for speculating on postage stamps, tries to rebel against the system.

candidates.title: The Prize of Peril
candidates.overview: In a futuristic society, contestants pit their survival skills against each other in a fight to the death for cash prizes, and the contest is aired live on television.

candidates.title: The Idealist
candidates.overview: A whistle blower attempts to reveal the secret behind a nuclear disaster that occurred during the height of the Cold War.

candidates.title: Stereo (Tile 3B of a CAEE Educational Mosaic)
candidates.overview: A group of Canadian university students agree to partake in a grisly psychological experiment, which renders them incapable of speech but able to communicate telepathically.

candidates.title: Your Lucky Day
candidates.overview: After a dispute over a winning lottery ticket turns into a deadly hostage situation, the witnesses must decide exactly how far they’ll go—and how much blood they’re willing to spill—for a cut of the $156 million.
